subject: Post-call: Finovate streaming & throughput qualification — routing and cost levers
messages:
From: Rebecca Zhao <r.zhao@finovate.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.l@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finovate.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick post-call notes — streaming & throughput

Thanks Jasmine — good call today. A few clarifications from our side so you have concrete numbers to qualify against: 

- Workload profile: mix of short-form prompts (avg 40 tokens out, 60 tokens in) for 75% of traffic and long-form generation (avg 600 tokens out) for 25% 
- Peak observed QPS: ~420 requests/sec during demo spikes (we expect to size for 500 qps peak 10% headroom)
- Concurrency: we typically have 30 concurrent live sessions, but spikes to 90 concurrent when marketing pushes run 
- Streaming expectation: low startup latency — users expect first token <120ms p95; subsequent tokens streamed at ~18–25 tokens/s felt-rate
- Cost sensitivity: target ~20–30% reduction versus our current hosting bill

Questions for the next steps: can you map which levers (continuous batching / prefix caching / quantization / model variants / region routing) move latency vs cost vs tail risk? Also want a short plan for canarying any quantized models — we cannot tolerate hallucination regressions.

Attachment: I uploaded a simple CSV with the sample QPS distribution — finovate_perf_matrix_v1.csv

Best,
Rebecca
Senior Product Manager
Finovate.ai
From: jasmine_liu <jasmine.l@redwood.ai>
To: Rebecca Zhao <r.zhao@finovate.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@finovate.ai>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.b@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 18:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick post-call notes — streaming & throughput

Rebecca — great detail, thanks. Sharing an internal sketch of how we’d approach qualification and the specific levers that most directly map to your targets. Marcus (SE) will lead the latency/streaming experiments; copying Lauren for rollout authority. High level: 

1) Immediate qualification matrix (week 0–1): Marcus to run a focused perf run against a representative traffic mix you provided (we'll use your CSV). Deliverables: p50/p95/p99 for first-token and full-response for three model variants (base-large, base-medium-quantized, small-optimized) and a baseline cost estimate.

2) Levers & expected impact (summary):
  - Continuous batching: improves throughput efficiency at the expense of a small added single-request scheduling delay. Expect 15–40% reduction in token cost at >200 qps. Good for your peak 500 qps window when paired with autoscale.
  - Prefix/KV caching: massive wins on repeat-session patterns. If 35% of tokens hit cache, effective cost per logical request drops ~20–35% and p95 tail improves because we short‑circuit computation. Requires warmup/TTL tuning.
  - Quantization profiles (int8 / mixed int8/16): meaningful cost drop (25–50% on GPU seconds) but introduces a small accuracy risk. We'll run evals on your red-team prompt set to quantify delta.
  - Model variants & routing: use small-optimized for short-form, large for long-form; edge routing to lower-latency regions for EU/US split. Dynamic fallback to larger model only if quality checks fail. This yields best latency-cost tradeoff.

3) Streaming-specific notes:
  - First-token target: 120ms p95 is tight but achievable with 1) warm KV cache, 2) pre-warmed transformers instances for hot routes, and 3) optimized kernel selection for short sequences.
  - Sustained token rhythm: we can cap token emission rates (throttling) to keep GPU utilization steady — configurable per route.

4) Canary & quality guardrails:
  - Progressive rollout: run A/B on 5% traffic with automated quality checks (prompt set pass-rate threshold) before ramp to 25/50/100%.
  - Auto-fallback: if perplexity/fuzzy-match/regression alerts trip, traffic shifts back to baseline model and we capture traces for triage.

Next steps: Marcus will schedule the perf run — can we confirm a 2-hour test window this week (preferably Wed AM PST)? If you can provide a 10–20 prompt eval set that captures failure modes, we'll include that in the quantization checks.

Thanks — attaching a one‑page proposed rollout (proposed_rollout_plan.pdf) for Lauren’s sign-off.

— Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.l@redwood.ai>, Rebecca Zhao <r.zhao@finovate.ai>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@finovate.ai>

Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick post-call notes — streaming & throughput

Rebecca / Samir — I built a quick test plan and resource estimate. High level technical asks and assumptions before the run: 

Assumptions from your numbers: target peak 500 qps, concurrency target 90, streaming first-token p95 target 120ms. We'll simulate the 75/25 short/long mix you described.

Technical asks for the test:
- Provide a representative 1000-request CSV with labels (short|long) and 15–20 red-team eval prompts for hallucination/accuracy checks.
- Which model family do you want as the baseline (please confirm: open-model-LLaMA-like-large or opt-3b-equivalent)?

Planned runs:
A) Baseline run (no quantization, no caching, conservative batching) — measure raw p50/p95/p99 and GPU seconds per request
B) Continuous batching enabled (batch size tuned to keep p95 <= 200ms) — measure cost delta
C) Prefix caching enabled (30/60/90s TTL variants) — measure cache hit-rate and effective cost
D) Quantized profile (int8) with eval checks — run A/B against baseline on a 5% traffic slice and capture regression metrics
E) Model routing experiment: route short-form to small-optimized, long-form to large, observe blended latency & cost

Estimated cluster time: 4 hours, using 8xA100-like GPUs for realistic tail behavior. Cost estimate to run tests in our lab: ~$1,400 (we can bill to RD-PO or include in POC credit).

I can run Wed 08:00–12:00 PST or Thu 09:00–13:00 PST. Please confirm slot and upload the CSV + eval prompts to the Drive link you already have.

— Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Rebecca Zhao <r.zhao@finovate.ai>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, jasmine_liu <jasmine.l@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@finovate.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.b@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Quick post-call notes — streaming & throughput

Thanks Marcus — Wed 08:00 PST works. We'll upload the 1000-row CSV and a 20-prompt eval set to the Drive by EOD today. 

Baseline model: prefer "open-llm-large-v2" as the baseline. For quantization canary, we'll accept a conservative int8 profile as long as you run the evals and send us the diff report. On canaries: we'll start at 3% traffic if the first A/B passes.

Two smaller asks: 
1) On autoscaling: if we see a sudden 2x spike from 100->200 qps for 30s, can we guarantee no dropped streams (i.e., graceful degrade to queued short responses)?
2) On observability: need token-level cost breakdown and per-request trace IDs surfaced in the logs for our compliance team.

Looking forward to Wed. Rebecca
